rows.name: trigger?
rows.notes: Handed to `PopoverTrigger` as `render` — never as its children. Optional, and the header says why: a popover driven from a store, or anchored at something that never opened it, has none.

rows.name: title?
rows.notes: The surface's visible heading, and its accessible name once the machine has read the part. Optional: left out, no title part is placed and the machine names the surface from `label` instead — the two are exclusive, and this is the form that keeps `label` reachable. `null` and `false` are excluded because `ReactNode` admits them and `title={cond && "…"}` would otherwise place an *empty* `h2` — which is worse than no title: the machine reads the part, flips `hasTitle`, and points `aria-labelledby` at an element with nothing in it, so the surface loses the `label` it would otherwise have been named by. The empty string cannot be excluded by a type (`Exclude<string, "">` is still `string`) and is treated as absent at the placement below instead.

rows.name: description?
rows.notes: Wired to `aria-describedby` by the machine, once it has read the part.

rows.name: children?
rows.notes: The body of the surface: the form, the list, the row of buttons.

rows.name: closeLabel?
rows.notes: Names the close button, and the part is placed only when it is given — see the header. Rendered empty, so the sheet paints the ✕.

rows.name: keepMounted?
rows.notes: Re-declared rather than inherited: the mount is the adapter's, not the machine's, so it lives on `PopoverRootProps` and not on `PopoverMachineProps`. Forwarded through the rest, the way `select` and `menu` forward theirs.
